description: spawn plugin hooks. UserPromptSubmit runs job-report.sh, which reports two things about the CURRENT worktree. FIRST, bg-agent jobs that reached a terminal state and have not been announced before, each marked so it is never announced twice. This exists because commands/bg-agent.md promised 'a notification when it reaches a terminal state' while bg-agent.sh's own comment said there was no channel to push one down — three jobs died unannounced on 2026-08-12, one of them an adversarial review of a PR that then merged without it. SECOND, team runs recorded under .spawn/teams, because a team's members run in SIBLING worktrees and so never reach this hook individually — the run record is what announces. A team run reports two ways: a LIVE one-line summary that is never marked and therefore repeats on every prompt for as long as the run is going, and one DONE announcement per run — not per member — that is marked and fires exactly once. The hook emits ONLY measured fields (terminal_state, deliverables_satisfied, alias, handle, denial count; for a run: resolved member states, progress against the pre-run baseline, the record's own verdict, counts and stop reasons) and NEVER the `narrative`, which is untrusted third-party model prose the rest of the plugin works to keep separate — injecting it here would hand that model a direct channel into the user's session. Raw stdout is the UserPromptSubmit injection channel (the seeded-recall.sh precedent). Fail-open in every path and exits 0 always: no git, no jq, no worktree, an unparseable record, an unwritable marker, or a roster larger than the render's bound all produce silence rather than a delayed or blocked prompt — silence is the designed failure mode, because the timeout below is the whole budget and rendering a run probes one member at a time. SPAWN_REPORT_MAX_MEMBERS and SPAWN_REPORT_MAX_RUNS set those bounds. Paths resolve via ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}; hook arrays merge additively with the user's settings and other plugins.
